plan.contextChunk: This figure is a labeled anatomy diagram of a horizontal ellipse, drawn as a blue outline centered at the origin of a coordinate system whose horizontal axis is marked x at the right and whose vertical axis is marked y at the top, both ending in arrowheads. A red dashed segment lies along the horizontal axis and spans the full width of the curve; the words "Major Axis" sit below its left half, and its two endpoints, where the outline meets the horizontal axis, are marked with dots and labeled "Vertex" at each end. A second red dashed segment lies along the vertical axis and spans the height of the curve, labeled "Minor Axis" beside its upper half, with black dots at its ends labeled "Co-vertex" above and "Co-vertex" below. The black dot where the two dashed segments cross is labeled "Center." Two small green dots sit on the horizontal dashed segment, one on either side of the center and well inside the vertices, each labeled "Focus." Collecting every named part on a single outline lets the reader tie each term to a definite position relative to the center. The diagram supplies the vocabulary needed to set up and read the standard equation of an ellipse.

interactionPlan.concept: Every named part of an ellipse — center, vertices, co-vertices, foci, major and minor axes — is fixed by two parameters, the semi-major axis a and semi-minor axis b, with the foci at distance c = √(a² − b²) from the center.

black dots at the left and right ends of the major axis, each labeled 'Vertex'
black dots at the top and bottom ends of the minor axis, each labeled 'Co-vertex'
black dot at the intersection of the axes, labeled 'Center'
two green dots on the major axis, one on each side of the center inside the vertices, each labeled 'Focus'

interactions.label: Semi-major axis a
interactions.teaches: The semi-major axis a controls the ellipse's width: the vertices and the full major axis stretch or shrink horizontally while the center stays fixed at the origin

interactions.label: Semi-minor axis b
interactions.teaches: The semi-minor axis b controls the ellipse's height: the co-vertices and minor axis move vertically while the vertices stay put, and as b approaches a the ellipse becomes nearly circular

interactions.label: Labels
interactions.teaches: The vocabulary of the figure maps directly onto the standard equation: vertex distance is a, co-vertex distance is b, and focus distance is c = √(a² − b²)

demo_steps.title: Anatomy of the ellipse
demo_steps.narration: The ellipse is built from two perpendicular dashed axes meeting at the center: the major axis ends at the vertices, the minor axis at the co-vertices, and the two foci sit inside the vertices on the major axis.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the width with a
demo_steps.narration: Drag a: the vertices slide outward and the major axis lengthens, and notice the foci are dragged along with them — widening the ellipse pushes the foci apart.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the height with b
demo_steps.narration: Drag b: only the co-vertices and minor axis move. As b nears a the ellipse rounds toward a circle and the foci converge on the center; as b shrinks the ellipse flattens and the foci approach the vertices.

demo_steps.title: Names become parameters
demo_steps.narration: Switch to equation parameters: the center-to-vertex distance is a, center-to-co-vertex is b, and center-to-focus is c = √(a² − b²) — the named anatomy is exactly what the standard equation x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 encodes.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The entire geometry of a centered horizontal ellipse is determined by a and b alone — vertices at (±a, 0), co-vertices at (0, ±b), and foci at (±c, 0) with c = √(a² − b²).
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Blue ellipse outline centered at the origin on light x/y axes with arrowheads (x label right, y label top). Red dashed horizontal and vertical segments span the ellipse's full width and height, meeting at a black center dot. Black dots at vertices (axis ends) and co-vertices; two green focus dots on the major axis inside the vertices, placed symmetrically at distance c = √(a² − b²) from center. Labels in italic serif textbook style: 'Vertex' at each end outside the curve, 'Co-vertex' above top and below bottom, 'Focus' above each green dot, 'Center' beside the origin, 'Major Axis' below the left half of the horizontal dashed line, 'Minor Axis' beside the upper half of the vertical dashed line. When sliders move a or b, ellipse, dashed axes, dots, and labels must all update together, and foci must reposition via c = √(a² − b²) (if b ≥ a, clamp or note the major axis would switch orientation). In equation-parameter mode, replace name labels with small 'a', 'b', 'c' annotations along the center-to-vertex, center-to-co-vertex, and center-to-focus half-segments, optionally showing the numeric values.

authoredContext:
Every ellipse has two axes of symmetry. The longer axis is called the major axis, and the shorter axis is called the minor axis. Each endpoint of the major axis is the vertex of the ellipse (plural: vertices), and each endpoint of the minor axis is a co-vertex of the ellipse. The center of an ellipse is the midpoint of both the major and minor axes. The axes are perpendicular at the center. The foci always lie on the major axis, and the sum of the distances from the foci to any point on the ellipse (the constant sum) is greater than the distance between the foci. See the figure.

A horizontal ellipse centered at (0, 0) in the x y coordinate system, with Major and Minor Axes, Vertices and Co-Vertices, Foci, and Center labeled.

In this section, we restrict ellipses to those that are positioned vertically or horizontally in the coordinate plane. That is, the axes will either lie on or be parallel to the x- and y-axes. Later in the chapter, we will see ellipses that are rotated in the coordinate plane.

discrepancies: the source draws arrowheads on both ends of each coordinate axis (left and right on x, up and down on y), but the generated figure only has arrowheads at the positive ends (right on x, top on y)
the default ellipse aspect ratio (a/b = 5/3 ≈ 1.7) is noticeably rounder than the source's more elongated shape (~2:1 between the vertex and co-vertex spans)
the 'y' axis label sits on the right of the y-axis in the generated figure, while the source places it on the left of the upward arrow
the right 'Vertex' label slightly overlaps the ellipse outline where the source keeps it fully clear of the curve
evaluation.notes: All anatomical elements (ellipse, dashed major/minor axes, vertices, co-vertices, foci, center) are present with correct colors and labels, and the sliders, label-mode toggle, step player, and dot popups are all genuinely functional and pedagogically apt; only minor fidelity issues remain — missing negative-end axis arrowheads, a slightly rounder default ellipse, and small label-placement deviations.
action_items: Add arrowheads to the negative ends of the coordinate axes (left on x, down on y) so both axis ends terminate in arrows as in the source — and clean up the messy duplicate-polygon cleanup code that currently leaves a possibly double-drawn right x-axis arrowhead.
Change the default b from 3 to ~2.4–2.5 (with a = 5) so the opening ellipse matches the source's more elongated ~2:1 proportions instead of the rounder 5:3.
Move the 'y' axis label to the left of the vertical axis and nudge the right 'Vertex' label a few more pixels outward so it no longer touches the ellipse curve.
